summary: Module 1 CONTEXT micro-exercise: three things to do BEFORE opening an AI agent for 'add team invitations to Team Collaboration'. (1) Map the existing data model and auth contract: read the actual schema (in this fork: models.py User/Link/ClickEvent, auth via JWT Bearer with a deps.py get_current_user, roles are not yet modeled) so the prompt describes REAL tables and relationships, not typical ones -- the Capable Intern will invent a users.teams table otherwise. (2) Identify the routing and validation patterns to follow: check how existing routers are organized (auth.py, links.py, redirect.py under app/routers), how schemas are validated (schemas/link.py pydantic models with Field constraints), and how errors are centralized (errors.py envelope + main.py exception handlers) -- the invitation endpoints must match these conventions, and the prompt must say 'use the existing pattern' rather than 'invent a new one'. (3) Pin the product constraints that the feature must satisfy before any prompt: from the canonical scenario -- invite flow must prevent unauthorized acceptance and replay-style abuse (so I need to decide: unique invite token, expiry, one-time-use semantics, who can accept), role enforcement must be explicit and verifiable on every protected action (so I need the role model and permission matrix defined first), and audit log entries for invite/accept actions must be complete enough for investigation (so I need to define what fields an audit entry records). These three preparations convert the prompt from 'add team invitations' into a spec the AI can satisfy and I can verify. The answer to 'what is NOT on the list' is open-the-agent-and-type-the-feature: that produces plausible-but-assumption-laden output built on what is typical, not what is true in this codebase.
evidence: Pre-prompt prep: data model read (models.py), routing/schema/error patterns identified (routers/, schemas/, errors.py)
Product constraints pinned: replay-safe invite flow, explicit role enforcement, complete audit entries
Capable Intern mental model applied: context-first, not prompt-first
